applies_why: The judge text resolves the D5/C1 collision by comparing the defender's and challenger's chains and declaring neither chain forces the other, which is the chain-against-chain weighing K-C governs.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'weighs chain against chain by footing': one reading requires resolving every collision to a winner, while the other permits an underdetermined result when neither chain forces the other.
why: The judge treated the collision as a contest between the defender's and challenger's chains and concluded neither forces the other, rather than using a verse-by-verse stating-verse test, so it complies with K-C.
